reuse.why: Routes all five planning sites through the existing getScheduledAmount and uses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance, but the API model writes its own expectedScheduleAmount instead of calling the helper.

duplication.why: api-models.ts expectedScheduleAmount duplicates the null/number/range resolution already in getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts where the tree keeps it; the API-only copy sits in api-models.ts outside that layer.

scope.why: Changes are limited to amount resolution, its callers, the API field and tests.

maintainability.why: The shared helper is clean, but the API copy was not updated by the later steps, so the API reports furthest-from-zero and ignores approx while the rest of the app uses the lowest value.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal uses a private expectedScheduleAmount instead of getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount, false, schedule._amountOp).

disguised_duplication.where: expectedScheduleAmount in api-models.ts restates getScheduledAmount's dispatch under another name with an abs-comparison endpoint choice.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter and an isapprox branch (both reasonable); api-models.ts toExternal bypasses it with its own copy, which drifts from the step 4 rule.
